$comment: data-color-grading payloads (HyperFrames realtime grading). Tested on the mop-star-trailer job: cold read about 20% less saturated than source, warm about 10% brighter with stronger color.

trailer-cold.use: Mock-epic or dramatic opening before a music drop: cool, muted, darker.

trailer-warm.use: Energy after a drop: warm, punchy, light grain and vignette.

mono.use: Black and white for a held breath (Adits Suspense Build visuals.bnw).

dark.use: Obscured opening that a reveal brightens out of (Adits Reveal, isolated dark areas).

teal-orange.use: Cinematic look (style-cinematic-long / -short): teal shadows, warm highlights, a little contrast, light grain. Colour wheels from the HyperFrames wheels example. Rendered in a 6 s test job (2026-10-14, HyperFrames 0.8.143); on a bright studio clip it showed mostly as the vignette. Not yet seen on dark footage.

natural-film.use: Cinematic finish that keeps the footage colours (style-cinematic-long / -short): a touch of contrast, soft vignette, light grain, no colour shift. Use after shots are colour matched. Rendered in a 6 s test job (2026-10-14, HyperFrames 0.8.143).
